## Second-implementation check
  every test accuracy recomputed from saved scores and regenerated labels equals the logged value

## Reading (written by hand after the generated part; the registered reading rules are in the prereg)

### Point 1: a label-free projection with an anti-collapse term does not match the naming head in any arena
- **No label-free arm reaches MATCH in any arena.**
  - Arena A: the dev-chosen arm (InfoNCE between each mention and the same mention in a reshuffled rendering of the
    instance, lambda 100) reaches 0.763 [0.741-0.785] (seeds 0.777 / 0.744 / 0.769). That recovers 63% of the gap
    between the probe floor (0.509) and the naming head (0.914): PARTIAL.
  - Trained for 30 epochs instead of 10 (exploratory run 1), it plateaus at 0.767 [0.745-0.788] (recovery 0.64), with
    training accuracy 0.95-0.99. More training does not close the gap.
  - The orthogonality arm gives 0.575 (FAIL) and the VICReg arm 0.503 (FAIL).
- **Arena B: FAIL for every family.** The dev-chosen arm (InfoNCE, candidates projected) gives 0.826
  [0.805-0.845], against floor 0.815 and naming head 0.996 (recovery 0.06).
  - InfoNCE and orth peak after one epoch, VICReg after 2-4. All three then fall to the majority rate on the
    held-out test pairs (final epoch 0.506 in every seed), while training accuracy is 0.95-1.00.
  - The label-free projections fit the training pairs and do not transfer to held-out (role, filler) pairs. The
    naming head and exact codes do (0.996).
- **Arena C: FAIL for every family** (orth 0.527, VICReg 0.504, InfoNCE 0.512, against floor 0.515 and naming head
  0.934).
- **What is missing is consistency, not separation.** This is checked by the cross-talk geometry on test, where symbol
  labels are used for the measurement only.
  - The orthogonality and InfoNCE terms do separate the codes. Different-symbol cosine is 0.03 (C orth), 0.08-0.11
    (A and B, orth and InfoNCE) and 0.12-0.22 (C InfoNCE), against 0.99 for the published binding-loss arm. That is
    under the 0.25 tolerance of the cross-talk sweep.
  - VICReg leaves the codes collapsed in A (0.93-0.97) and half-collapsed in B (0.44-0.57); in C it gives 0.15-0.19.
  - But the codes of the same symbol in different places do not agree. Same-symbol cosine is 0.22-0.37 in C,
    0.57-0.72 in A (orth, InfoNCE) and 0.73-0.81 in B, where the naming head and exact codes give 1.
  - In C one symbol is written in decimal as a filler and in hex as a role, and nothing label-free links the two.
    C's same-symbol cosine is the lowest (0.22-0.37), and every C family stays within 0.02 of the floor on test.
  - In A every mention of a symbol has the same surface form, and InfoNCE gets furthest there.
- **Reading under the registered rules:**
  - The failure of the published binding-loss arm is not only collapse. Anti-collapse fixes the collapse, but
    without an identity signal the frozen states do not give codes consistent enough for the memory.
  - Identity labels (or exact symbols) remain necessary in B and C. In A a label-free contrastive code gets about
    two thirds of the way there.

### Point 2: the tuned fine-tune
- **Margins against the naming head:**

  | arena | tuned fine-tune | published fine-tune | margin (published) | outcome |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | A | 0.500 [0.476-0.523] | 0.505 | +0.414 (+0.408) | STANDS |
  | B | 0.878 [0.859-0.896] | 0.795 | +0.118 (+0.201) | NARROWED |
  | C | 0.482 [0.463-0.500] | 0.516 | +0.452 (+0.418) | STANDS |

  - Per-seed margins: A +0.400 / +0.424 / +0.418; C +0.452 / +0.460 / +0.444; B +0.086 / +0.020 / +0.248.
- **No arena counts as "fitted" under the registered rule** (training accuracy >= 0.95 in tuning and in every final
  seed), so all three carry the "under-fitted baseline" label.
  - **A:** the best training accuracy over 9 lr x schedule configurations at 12 epochs is 0.549. The 30-epoch stage-3
    run of the configuration closest to fitting reaches 0.732, with dev 0.488-0.532.
  - **C:** the best 12-epoch training accuracy is 0.574. The 30-epoch stage-3 run memorises to 0.881 while dev stays
    at 0.514-0.544.
  - **B:** the fine-tune learns the task. In tuning (seed 42): dev 0.996, training 0.999. In the finals all three seeds
    leave the one-class plateau, but late: dev first exceeds 0.70 at epoch 8, 7 and 8. Two seeds end at training
    0.928 and 0.777 when the cosine schedule runs out.
- **Where a fine-tune comes closest to fitting A and C, the extra training-split accuracy buys no dev accuracy.**
  Stage 3: A training 0.51 -> 0.73 with dev <= 0.53; C training 0.51 -> 0.88 with dev <= 0.54. That is memorising,
  not learning the composition.
- **So the registered reading:**
  - A and C: the margin stands. But the paper may not say that no fine-tune can learn A or C. It may say that a
    fine-tune tuned over learning rate (5 values), schedule (2) and epochs (12-30) on the same 2,000 / 800 training
    instances did not learn them, and that the runs which came closest to fitting were memorising.
  - B: the published +0.20 shrinks to +0.12, and a fine-tune can learn B outright (0.980 in one final seed; 0.994 on
    dev with the published fp32 configuration). B belongs with "a tuned fine-tune can learn the task, unreliably".

### Predictions that failed
- **Label-free A:** predicted FAIL, measured PARTIAL. A contrastive code from reshuffled views does much better than
  predicted in the arena where surface forms repeat.
- **Label-free B:** predicted PARTIAL, measured FAIL. Overfitting to the training pairs, not collapse, ends it.
- **qc = proj in C:** predicted for every family; VICReg's dev choice used index.
- **The fine-tune fits its training split in every arena:** failed in all three (see above). This includes "C fits by
  memorising (training >= 0.95)": training reached only 0.881 at 30 epochs.
- **Fine-tune on B >= 0.95 in every seed:** measured 0.904 / 0.980 / 0.750. B was predicted CLOSED and is NARROWED.
- **Held:** G0; label-free C FAIL; no label-free MATCH; the C label-free geometry (separation without consistency);
  qc = proj in B; the A and C fine-tune ceilings (<= 0.70 and <= 0.65); Point 2 STANDS on A and C.

### Checks from other angles
- **Gates:** the original run functions reproduce all 24 banked G0a cells exactly. The new code path with the
  regulariser off reproduces the 9 banked binding-loss cells exactly (G0b), on the cached frozen states. The B27
  arms are therefore comparable with the published ones.
- **Second implementation:** every test accuracy was recomputed from the saved per-instance scores, thresholds and
  labels regenerated from the generators, and equals the logged value.
- **Determinism:**
  - Seed 42's final LoRA runs reproduce their tuning runs exactly in A and C (dev identical to 3 decimals for all 12
    epochs).
  - In B the identical configuration escaped the plateau at epoch 5 in tuning and at epoch 8 in the final run.
    Near the escape, small nondeterministic GPU differences grow, so B's fine-tune result has a large run-to-run
    spread. The published B spread (0.980 / 0.895 / 0.510) is consistent with the same cause.
- **Readout diagnostic (CPU, train and dev only, b27_out/logs/diag_probe.txt):** Phi-2's final state at the last
  token is nearly the same vector for every input (mean pairwise cosine 0.95-0.98, norm 50-62). Consistent with
  anisotropy (Ethayarajh 2019) and massive activations (Sun et al. 2024).
  - A linear head on the raw state (Adam, 2,000 full-batch steps) fits A's training split only to 0.735.
    Standardised, it fits all three (1.000), with dev at chance on A and C.
  - The published fine-tune's training accuracy of 0.50-0.53 is the same one-class plateau seen here at most learning
    rates. Escaping it depends on the rate and schedule (constant 2e-4: B dev 0.962 after one epoch; 3e-4 or 1e-3:
    one class for 12 epochs).
  - This matches the BERT fine-tuning literature: failed runs are optimisation failures, and small step sizes with
    more iterations fix them (Mosbach et al. 2021; Dodge et al. 2020).
- **The published fp32 / attention-only / batch-2 configuration, rerun on the B27 1,000-instance B split (train and
  dev only):** dev 0.980 after one epoch and 0.994 after two. The published fine-tune could learn B; its 0.510 seed
  was a plateau that did not break.
- **B's floor is weak:** a standardised linear probe on B's frozen last-token state reaches 0.922 on B dev, against
  the paper's 0.815 floor (raw state, 2 epochs). The registered bars keep the banked floor. Against 0.922 the B
  label-free arms would be further below.
- **Literature:**
  - Supports the label-free result: contrastive learning keeps only what the views share (InfoMin; Tian et al.,
    NeurIPS 2020). Our views share each mention's surface form and partner, so the code becomes consistent across
    contexts only where a symbol's surface form repeats (A). It cannot link decimal and hex forms of one symbol (C),
    and it learns pair-specific features that do not transfer to held-out pairs (B).
  - Supports the fine-tune result: small transformers trained directly on search and multi-step retrieval learn it
    only with large, carefully balanced data, and less so as inputs grow (Saparov et al., ICLR 2025, "Transformers
    struggle to learn to search"; Zhang et al. 2021, pointer value retrieval). 2,000 and 800 instances are small by
    that standard.
  - Collapse without an anti-collapse term (V-165) is the standard outcome in self-supervised learning (SimCLR, BYOL,
    VICReg).
  - No conflicting result found.

### Deviations and what went wrong (all before any LoRA selection or test run; each in a dated, committed amendment)
- **Amendment 1 (fixed standardisation of the LoRA head input):** did not lift the plateau. Withdrawn.
- **Amendment 2 (30-epoch tuning over lr {1e-3, 1e-4}):** dropped the rates that work. Withdrawn after a B diagnostic.
- **Amendment 3:** back to the registered protocol.
- **Amendment 4:** the published constant schedule added as a tuned factor.
- **Stopped runs:** six LoRA runs (pre-amendment, amendment 1) and four (amendment 2), plus smokes and diagnostics.
  About 6 GPU-hours, all counted.
- **Stage 2 (rank 4 and 64) was cut** under the registered budget order, so rank was not tuned. The paper should say
  so.
- **Stage-1b edge runs** were run as registered (lr 1e-5; for A in the constant schedule, after one cosine 1e-5 run
  was stopped as the wrong schedule).
- **The arena-A label-free finals** were restarted per seed on three GPUs after 9 of 30 epochs on one shared GPU.
  The code path is deterministic (gates exact).
- **Exploratory run 1** (A InfoNCE, 30 epochs) was registered as exploratory before its test was read; reported
  beside, not instead of, the registered result.
- **Compute:** 37.3 GPU-hours on the A800 box (cap 40). PACE was not used: earliest starts were 11-22 and 11-23.
